steps: On count 1, bend the elbows, lowering the body until the upper arms are parallel to the ground. At the same time, raise the left leg until the toe is level or just above the right heel. Keep the left knee straight. This is not a high leg raise or hyper-extension of the hip.
On count 2, reverse the movement performed in count 1 to return to the starting position.
On count 3, repeat count 1, moving the right leg the same way that the left leg moved in count 1.
On count 4, return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Tuck
exercises.about: The Single-Leg Tuck is the fourth exercise in the Hip Stability Drill. Figure 4-4 on page 4-4 shows the exercise Soldiers perform it in a formation at a slow cadence:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Single-Leg Tuck is the Sitting position. Soldiers move to a side lying position, with legs extended, the left leg is held 6–8 inches above the right.
steps: Support the trunk off the ground with the right elbow. Bend the elbow to 90 degrees and place it directly below the shoulder. Fist the right hand and rest it on the ground, thumb up. Place the left hand across the stomach.

On the count of 1, bend the left knee and hip to 90 degrees, holding the leg and foot in the same plane throughout the movement. Control the movement to the end point. The left foot and knee should be the same height from the ground to work the correct muscles in the hip. Do not let the foot drop to the ground.
On count 2, return to the starting position.
On count 3, repeat count 1.
On count 4, return to the first starting position.
Repeat 5–10 times.

On the command, “CHANGE POSITION, MOVE,” swing the legs together toward the front of the formation, swiveling on the buttocks into the second starting position with the trunk supported on the left elbow.
Complete the same series of repetitions for the right leg and hip.

exercises.name: Squat Bender
exercises.about: The Squat Bender (see figure 3-7) is the fifth exercise in the Preparation Drill. This exercise develops strength, endurance, and flexibility in the lower back and thigh muscles. It prepares Soldiers to use proper lifting technique in more vigorous training and testing events that require heavy lifts. Soldiers conduct the movement at a slow cadence:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Squat Bender is the Straddle Stance position with hands on hips.
steps: On count 1, squat while leaning slightly forward from the waist, keeping the head up and moving both arms to a position in front of the body and parallel to the ground. Palms face inwards.
On count 2, reverse the movement performed in count 1 to return to the starting position.

On count 3, with the knees slightly bent, bend forward at the waist. Maintain the head in alignment with the spine and keep the spine straight. Reach toward the ground until a stretch is felt in the back of the thighs.
On count 4, return to the starting position.
exercises.dose: Perform 5–10 repetitions.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pull
exercises.equipment_said: On the command, “UP,” move from the starting position, keep the arms straight, and pull the body up with the effect of raising the head between the arms. The chest will move up toward the bar and the shoulder blades will move together.
exercises.about: The Straight-Arm Pull is the first exercise in Climbing Drill 1. This exercise develops the Soldier’s ability to initiate the pull-up motion, maintain grip, and contract upper back and shoulder muscles. Figure 6-1 on page 6-2 breaks down the exercise as Soldiers conduct it with two spotters:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Straight-Arm Pull is the Straight-Arm Hang using the closed overhand grip.
steps: On the command, “UP,” move from the starting position, keep the arms straight, and pull the body up with the effect of raising the head between the arms. The chest will move up toward the bar and the shoulder blades will move together.
On the command, “DOWN,” return to the starting position.
exercises.dose: Repeat the exercise 5–10 times.
notes: If the Soldier states “No spotter needed,” the two spotters are not required. Otherwise, the spotters assume the Straddle Stance position with staggered legs in front and behind the exerciser.
The front spotter places palms toward the exerciser at chest height to support the exerciser if his or her grip fails.

The rear spotter places palms toward the exerciser at chest height to support the exerciser if his or her grip fails. The rear spotter assists in guiding the exerciser to the foot pegs on the climbing bar.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pull
exercises.about: The Straight-Arm Pull is the alternate fifth exercise in the Strength Training Circuit. This exercise develops the Soldier’s ability to pull up without using the legs. Figure 13-6 shows the exercise as it would be conducted by an individual Soldier during the Strength Training Circuit:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Straight Arm Pull is the Straight-Arm Hang using the closed overhand grip.
steps: After repeating 5 times, dismount to the Straddle Stance position on the ground.
On count 1, from the starting position and keeping the arms straight, pull the body up using a shrugging motion.
exercises.dose: Repeat the exercise for up to one minute.

exercises.name: Straight-Leg Deadlift
exercises.equipment_said: Figure 14-5 breaks down the exercise as it would be conducted by an individual Soldier using a straight bar and dumbbells:
exercises.about: The Straight-Leg Deadlift is a variation of the Deadlift that further challenges the muscles in the lower back, hips, and legs. Figure 14-5 breaks down the exercise as it would be conducted by an individual Soldier using a straight bar and dumbbells:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Straight-Leg Deadlift using the straight bar is the Straddle Stance position. Hold the bar with a grip suited to the Soldier’s capability, the equipment, and the goal of the exercise session. Keep the knees slightly flexed—not locked—and in the same flexed position throughout the exercise.
steps: From the starting position, flex forward from the waist, keeping the head aligned with the spine to avoid extending the neck.
While keeping the back straight, bend over until the back is parallel to the ground. Slightly adjust knee flexion to increase the engagement of the hamstring muscles in the back of the thigh.
After a brief pause, reverse the movement to return to the starting position.
Always lift a weight that can be controlled throughout the range of motion.
Use the same movement with different grips for the kettlebell and dumbbell versions of this exercise.
exercises.dose: Repeat this movement for the correct number of repetitions and sets required to meet the goal of the free weight session.

exercises.name: Straight-Leg Deadlift
exercises.equipment_said: The starting position for the Straight-Leg Deadlift is the Straddle Stance position. Hold the kettlebells in front of the legs using a pronated grip. Keep the knees slightly flexed—not locked—and in the same flexed position throughout the exercise.
exercises.about: The Straight-Leg Deadlift is the second exercise in the Strength Training Circuit (see figure 13-2). A Soldier conducts the exercise for one minute at station 2 of the Strength Training Circuit. The cadence is always slow:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Straight-Leg Deadlift is the Straddle Stance position. Hold the kettlebells in front of the legs using a pronated grip. Keep the knees slightly flexed—not locked—and in the same flexed position throughout the exercise.
steps: On count 1, flex forward from the waist, keeping the head in line with the spine to avoid extending the neck. While keeping the back straight, move down until the back is parallel to the ground. Slightly adjust knee flexion to increase the engagement of the hamstring muscles in the back of the thigh.
On count 2, reverse the movement performed in count 1 to return to the starting position.
On count 3, repeat count 1.
exercises.dose: Complete one minute of repetitions, stopping to rest if necessary, or adjusting the weight and range of movement to match the required performance.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.equipment_said: Figure 14-11 on page 14-10 illustrates a Soldier performing the exercise using two of the three types of free weights—straight bar, kettlebells, and dumbbells:
exercises.about: The Sumo Deadlift is a free-weight exercise performed throughout a Soldier’s career to improve lower body muscular strength and endurance. It is a modification of the Deadlift that further challenges a Soldier’s coordination, balance, and hip mobility. Figure 14-11 on page 14-10 illustrates a Soldier performing the exercise using two of the three types of free weights—straight bar, kettlebells, and dumbbells:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Sumo Deadlift is the Straddle Stance position with feet slightly wider than shoulder width and toes pointing outward. When performing the lift with dumbbells or kettlebells, start in the Straddle Stance position with a single weight held between and in front of the legs. Knees are bent, back is straight, and the bar or weight is held in both hands with a grip suited to the lifter’s capability, the equipment, and the goal of the exercise session.
steps: From the starting position, straighten the knees and slowly raise the trunk into the upright Position of Attention.
Pause before reversing the upward movement to return to the starting position.
Maintain a natural arch in the lower back with the head and neck staying in alignment to avoid extending the neck. Do not round out the upper back.
Keep the knees and feet turned outward throughout the movement. The wider stance permits a lower lifting range of motion.
Always lift a weight that can be controlled throughout the range of motion.
Use the same movement with different grips for the kettlebell and dumbbell versions.
exercises.dose: Repeat this movement for the correct number of repetitions and sets required to meet the goal of the free weight session.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat
exercises.equipment_said: Hold a single kettlebell with both hands in front of the body, palms pronated to face the body.
exercises.about: The Sumo Squat is the first exercise in the Strength Training Circuit. The starting position for the Sumo Squat is the Straddle Stance position with the feet slightly wider than the shoulders and the toes pointing outward. Hold a single kettlebell with both hands in front of the body, palms pronated to face the body. Figure 13-1 on page 13-2 shows the exercise as a Soldier conducts it for one minute at station 1 of the Strength Training Circuit. The cadence is always slow:
steps: On count 1, squat while leaning slightly forward from the waist with the head up. Move downward until the upper legs are parallel to the ground.
On count 2, reverse the movement performed in count 1 to return to the starting position.
On count 3, repeat count 1.
On count 4, return to the starting position.
exercises.dose: Complete one minute of repetitions, stopping to rest if necessary, or adjusting the weight and range of movement to match the required performance.

exercises.name: Supine Body Twist
exercises.equipment_said: The starting position for the Supine Body Twist is the Supine position with the hips and knees bent to 90 degrees so that the feet are off the ground. The head is off the ground. One kettlebell is held in front of and off the chest. The kettlebell handle is held by both hands, palms facing each other. The bell portion of the kettlebell is positioned above the stomach, not above the head.
exercises.about: The Supine Body Twist is the ninth exercise in the Strength Training Circuit. This exercise strengthens the trunk muscles used for movement in the transverse plane. By keeping the knees together it also strengthens hip adductor muscles often referred to as the groin muscles. Figure 13-10 shows the exercise as a Soldier conducts it for one minute at station 9 of the Strength Training Circuit:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Supine Body Twist is the Supine position with the hips and knees bent to 90 degrees so that the feet are off the ground. The head is off the ground. One kettlebell is held in front of and off the chest. The kettlebell handle is held by both hands, palms facing each other. The bell portion of the kettlebell is positioned above the stomach, not above the head.
steps: On the command, “BEGIN,” rotate the kettlebell to the left and the legs to the right as far as possible under control. Keep the weight away from the body and the arms and head off the ground.
Return to the starting position.
Repeat the first movement—this time to the opposite side—arms to the right and legs to the left.
The head may turn with the arms but should not lift more than 2–4 inches from the ground.
exercises.dose: Continue the exercise at own pace for one minute maintaining the range of motion. Increase or decrease the kettlebell weight if necessary, continuing only if the exercise can be completed to standard.

exercises.name: Supine Chest Press
exercises.equipment_said: Holding a kettlebell of the same weight in each hand using a closed partial pronated grip, bend the elbows to allow the kettlebells to rest on the front of the shoulders.
exercises.about: The Supine Chest Press is the sixth exercise in the Strength Training Circuit. This exercise strengthens the chest, shoulder, and triceps muscles. It develops the Soldier’s ability to push during more vigorous combatives, testing, and combat tasks. Figure 13-7 illustrates the exercise as a Soldier conducts it for one minute at station 6 of the Strength Training Circuit:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Supine Chest Press is the Supine position with knees bent to 90 degrees, feet 8–12 inches apart and flat on the ground. The head and upper arms are resting on the ground.
steps: Holding a kettlebell of the same weight in each hand using a closed partial pronated grip, bend the elbows to allow the kettlebells to rest on the front of the shoulders.
On the command, “BEGIN,” extend the elbows to raise the kettlebells straight up in front of the shoulders, rotating to a fully pronated grip.
Return to the starting position.
exercises.dose: Continue the exercise at own pace for one minute. Increase or decrease the kettlebell weight if necessary, continuing only if the Supine Chest Press movement can be completed to standard.

exercises.name: T Raise
exercises.about: The second exercise for the Shoulder Stability Drill is the T Raise. Figure 4-7 illustrates the exercise as performed in a formation at a slow cadence:
exercises.start: The starting position for the T Raise is the Prone position with arms laying on the ground straight out from the shoulders at 90 degrees to the trunk. This is the T position. The head is slightly elevated. Feet are together and toes are pointing rearward. Fingers and thumbs are extended and joined with palms perpendicular to the ground, facing directly ahead.
steps: On the count of 1, raise both arms from the ground 3–6 inches while continuing to keep the elbows straight. The head remains in its starting position.
On count 2, return to the starting position.
On count 3, repeat count 1.
On count 4, return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Thigh Stretch
exercises.about: The Thigh Stretch is the fourth exercise in the Recovery Drill. It develops flexibility in the hip and knee joints. Figure 16-4 shows the movement as Soldiers conduct it in a formation:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Thigh Stretch is the Sitting position with the arms at the sides and palms on the floor.
steps: On the command, “READY, STRETCH,” roll on the right side and place the right elbow and forearm on the ground directly below the shoulder. The right hand makes a fist with the thumb side up. Grasp the left ankle and pull toward the left buttock. Push the left thigh further to the rear with the heel of the right foot. Hold this position for 20–30 seconds.
On the command, “CHANGE POSITION, READY, STRETCH,” move back through the starting position before changing sides to stretch the right leg. Hold for 20–30 seconds.
On the command, “STARTING POSITION, MOVE,” return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Triceps Extension
exercises.equipment_said: Select the weight and ensure the pin is secure in the weight stack.
exercises.about: The Triceps Extension develops strength in the triceps muscles and supports other pushing tasks found in training and combat. Figure 15-14 breaks down the exercise as a Soldier conducts it:
steps: Select the weight and ensure the pin is secure in the weight stack.
Conduct this exercise from the Sitting position. Start with the feet placed firmly on the ground. Place the hips and low back firmly against the seat back with the eyes looking straight ahead.
Maintain an erect position, eyes looking straight ahead, grasping the bar with a closed, pronated grip.
On count 1, push downward until both arms are fully extended but not locked.
On count 2, return to the starting position.
exercises.dose: Repeat this movement for the correct number of repetitions and sets required to meet the goal of the strength machine session.

exercises.name: Trunk Extension
exercises.equipment_said: The starting position for the Trunk Extension is the Sitting position with the knees slightly bent and feet flat on the foot platform.
exercises.about: The Trunk Extension is the seventh exercise in the Strength Training Machine drill. This exercise develops strength in the low back muscles and supports the Deadlift exercise. Figure 15-13 on page 15-12 shows the exercise as a Soldier conducts it:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Trunk Extension is the Sitting position with the knees slightly bent and feet flat on the foot platform.
steps: From the starting position, stay seated on the machine, leaning slightly forward, with the back firmly against the padded lever arm.
Select the appropriate weight and ensure the pin is secure in the weight stack.
Grip the support bars using a neutral, closed grip.
Keep the head in a neutral position with the eyes looking straight ahead.
On count 1, raise the upper body and continue extending the trunk, moving to the Supine position.
On count 2, return to the starting position.
exercises.dose: Repeat this movement for the correct number of repetitions and sets required to meet the goal of the strength machine session.

exercises.name: Trunk Flexion
exercises.equipment_said: Select the appropriate weight and ensure the pin is secure in the weight stack.
exercises.about: The Trunk Flexion is the tenth exercise in the strength training machine drill. This exercise develops strength in the abdominal muscles. Figure 15-18 on page 15-16 shows the exercise as a Soldier conducts it:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Trunk Flexion is the Sitting position with the knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor.
steps: From the starting position, stay seated with the feet firmly on the ground.
Select the appropriate weight and ensure the pin is secure in the weight stack.
Keep the elbows shoulder-width apart and bent at 90 degrees, with hands in a closed grip.
Place the hips and low back firmly against the seat back with the eyes looking straight ahead.
On count 1, bend forward, flexing the trunk and bringing the chest to the thighs.
On count 2, return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Upright Row
exercises.equipment_said: It can be performed with a straight bar, dumbbells, or kettlebells.
exercises.about: The Upright Row is a modified version of the Bent-Over Row. It focuses the work on the upper trapezius as well as those muscles targeted in the Bent-Over Row. It can be performed with a straight bar, dumbbells, or kettlebells. Figures 14-15 and 14-16 on page 14-14 illustrate the exercise as it would be conducted by an individual Soldier using a straight bar and kettlebells:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Upright Row is the Straddle Stance position with arms fully extended and down in front of the body holding the straight bar or kettlebell with a closed overhand grip. A single weight or short bar can be used when first performing this exercise.
steps: From the starting position, pull the weight up to the collar bones until the arms are parallel to the ground.
After a brief pause, reverse the movement to return to the down position.
As the weight and repetitions increase, concentrate on preventing the upper back and shoulder from rounding forward.
Always lift a weight that can be controlled throughout the range of motion.
Use the same movement with neutral grips for the kettlebell version of this exercise.
exercises.dose: Repeat this movement for the correct number of repetitions and sets required to meet the goal of the free weight session.

exercises.name: V-Up
exercises.about: The V-Up is the second exercise in Conditioning Drill 1. This exercise develops the abdominal and hip flexor muscles for more vigorous training and combat tasks such as the leg tuck, rope traverse, and surmounting obstacles. Figure 5-2 breaks down the movement Soldier conduct at a moderate cadence:
exercises.start: The starting position for the V-Up is the Supine position with arms on the ground at 45 degrees from the body, knees bent to 90 degrees. The head is 1–2 inches off the ground.
steps: On count 1, raise the legs and trunk at the same time into a V position, using the arms to balance. Keep the knees straight and the head aligned with the trunk—neither bent forward nor extended backwards.
On count 2, return under control to the starting position. Avoid dropping the legs.
On count 3, repeat count 1.
On count 4, return to the count 2 position.

exercises.name: W Raise
exercises.about: The fifth exercise for the Shoulder Stability Drill is the W Raise. Figures 4-10 and 4-11 show the exercise as performed in a formation at a slow cadence:
exercises.start: The starting position for the W Raise is the Prone position with arms on the ground at 45 degrees to the trunk and elbows bent to 45 degrees. This is the W position. The head is slightly elevated. Feet are together and toes are pointing rearward. Fingers and thumbs are extended and joined with palms facing each other.
steps: On the count of 1, raise both arms from the ground 3–6 inches while continuing to keep the elbows bent. The head remains in its starting position. The elbows, forearms, and hands should leave the ground at the same time.
On count 2, return to the starting position.
On count 3, repeat count 1.
On count 4, return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Weighted Trunk Extension
exercises.equipment_said: Hold a weight plate against the chest before lowering the upper body toward the ground by flexing at the hips. This is the starting position.
exercises.about: The Weighted Trunk Extension develops strength in the muscles of the lower back and hips. It is performed using a bench and a partner. Figure 14-25 shows the exercise as a Soldier conducts it:
exercises.start: To reach the starting position for the Weighted Trunk Extension, lay in the Prone position on a trunk extension bench with the knees slightly flexed and feet anchored or on the end of a flat bench. A partner secures the exerciser’s legs at the calves or ankles.
steps: Hold a weight plate against the chest before lowering the upper body toward the ground by flexing at the hips. This is the starting position.
From the starting position, raise the upper body to align the trunk with the legs. When viewed from the side, the body and legs will form a straight line from the head to the heels.
The partner continues to brace the legs throughout the movement.
After a brief pause, reverse the movement lowering the body back down to the starting position.
Always lift a weight that can be controlled throughout the range of motion.
exercises.dose: Repeat this movement for the correct number of repetitions and sets required to meet the goal of the free weight session.

exercises.name: Weighted Trunk Flexion
exercises.equipment_said: Hold a dumbbell or plate in each hand, resting on the front of the chest.
exercises.about: The Weighted Trunk Flexion develops strength in the abdominal muscles to support trunk movement when the Soldier is wearing full uniform and protective equipment. Figure 14-24 shows the exercise as it would be conducted by an individual Soldier:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Weighted Trunk Flexion is the Supine position with knees bent to 90 degrees and feet on the ground. Feet are unanchored.
steps: Hold a dumbbell or plate in each hand, resting on the front of the chest.
From the starting position, raise the trunk up into a sitting position without shifting the feet and leg position.
After a brief pause, reverse the movement to return under control to the starting position.
Always use a weight that can be controlled throughout the range of motion.
Use a lighter weight to improve control if necessary.
exercises.dose: Repeat this movement for the correct number of repetitions and sets required to meet the goal of the free weight session.

exercises.name: Windmill
exercises.about: The Windmill (see figure 3-8 and figure 3-9) is the sixth exercise in the Preparation Drill. This exercise develops the ability to safely bend and simultaneously rotate the trunk. It requires flexibility in the spine and coordination of the shoulder girdle. It prepares Soldiers to use proper movement technique in more vigorous training, testing, and combat tasks. Soldiers conduct the movement at a slow cadence:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Windmill is the Straddle Stance position with arms straight out to the side. Fingers and thumbs are extended and joined, palms are facing down.
steps: On count 1, bend the hips and knees while rotating the trunk to the left. Reach down to touch the outside of the left foot with the right hand and look to the rear. The left arm is pulled rearward to maintain alignment across the shoulders with the right arm.
On count 2, reverse the movement performed in count 1 to return to the starting position.
On count 3, repeat count 1, this time to the right.
On count 4, return to the starting position.
exercises.dose: Perform 5–10 repetitions.

exercises.name: Y Raise
exercises.about: The third exercise for the Shoulder Stability Drill is the Y Raise. Figure 4-8 shows Soldiers performing the exercise in a formation at a slow cadence:
exercises.start: The starting position for the Y Raise is the Prone position with arms laying on the ground extended overhead at 45 degrees to the trunk. This is the Y position. The head is slightly elevated. Feet are together and toes are pointing rearward. Fingers and thumbs are extended and joined with palms facing each other.
steps: On the count of 1, raise both arms from the ground 3–6 inches while continuing to keep the elbows straight. The head remains in its starting position.
On count 2, return to the starting position.
On count 3, repeat count 1.
On count 4, return to the starting position.

exercises.name: Ankle stretch
exercises.ref: Sitting exercises · page last reviewed 18 January 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Sit upright, hold on to the side of the chair and straighten your left leg with your foot off the floor.
exercises.about: This stretch will improve ankle flexibility and lower the risk of developing a blood clot.
steps: Sit upright, hold on to the side of the chair and straighten your left leg with your foot off the floor.
With your leg straight and raised, point your toes away from you.
Point your toes back towards you.
exercises.dose: Try 2 sets of 5 stretches with each foot.

exercises.name: Biceps curls
exercises.ref: Strength exercises · page last reviewed 28 February 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Hold a pair of light weights (filled water bottles will do) and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
steps: Hold a pair of light weights (filled water bottles will do) and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Keeping your arms by your side, slowly bend them until the weight in your hand reaches your shoulder.
Slowly lower again.
exercises.dose: This can also be carried out while sitting. Attempt 3 sets of 5 curls with each arm.

exercises.name: Buttock stretch
exercises.ref: How to stretch after exercising · page last reviewed 16 March 2026
steps: Lie on your back and bring your knees up to your chest.
Cross your right leg over your left thigh.
Grasp the back of your left thigh with both hands.
Pull your left leg towards your chest.
Repeat with the opposite leg.
exercises.dose: hold for 15 to 20 seconds

exercises.name: Calf raises
exercises.ref: Strength exercises · page last reviewed 28 February 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Rest your hands on the back of a chair for stability.
steps: Rest your hands on the back of a chair for stability.
Lift both heels off the floor as far as is comfortable. The movement should be slow and controlled.
exercises.dose: Repeat 5 times.
notes: To make this more difficult, perform the exercise without support.

exercises.name: Calf stretch
exercises.ref: Flexibility exercises · page last reviewed 20 November 2023
exercises.equipment_said: Place your hands against a wall for stability. Bend the right leg and step the left leg back at least a foot's distance, keeping it straight. Both feet should be flat on the floor.
exercises.about: Good for loosening tight calf muscles.
steps: Place your hands against a wall for stability. Bend the right leg and step the left leg back at least a foot's distance, keeping it straight. Both feet should be flat on the floor.
The left calf muscle is stretched by keeping the left leg as straight as possible and the left heel on the floor.
Repeat with the opposite leg.
exercises.dose: Perform 3 on each side.

exercises.name: Calf stretch
exercises.ref: How to stretch after exercising · page last reviewed 16 March 2026
steps: Step your right leg forward, keeping it bent, and lean forwards slightly.
Keep your left leg straight and try to lower the left heel to the ground.
If you need to, lean on the back of a chair or on a wall to support yourself.
Repeat with the opposite leg.
exercises.dose: hold for 15 to 20 seconds

exercises.name: Chest stretch
exercises.ref: Sitting exercises · page last reviewed 18 January 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Sit upright and away from the back of the chair. Pull your shoulders back and down. Extend your arms out to the side.
exercises.about: This stretch is good for posture.
steps: Sit upright and away from the back of the chair. Pull your shoulders back and down. Extend your arms out to the side.
Gently push your chest forward and up until you feel a stretch across your chest.
exercises.dose: Hold for 5 to 10 seconds and repeat 5 times.

exercises.name: Hamstring stretch
exercises.ref: How to stretch after exercising · page last reviewed 16 March 2026
steps: Lie on your back and raise your right leg.
Hold your right leg with both hands, below your knee.
Keeping your left leg bent with your foot on the floor, pull your right leg towards you keeping it straight.
Repeat with the opposite leg.
exercises.dose: hold for 15 to 20 seconds

exercises.name: Hamstring stretch with thigh contraction
exercises.ref: Knee exercises for runners · page last reviewed 20 September 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Sit on the edge of a chair. Keep your right leg bent and straighten your left leg, placing the left heel on the ground with your foot pointing slightly outwards.
steps: Sit on the edge of a chair. Keep your right leg bent and straighten your left leg, placing the left heel on the ground with your foot pointing slightly outwards.
Keeping your back straight, bend towards your left leg to stretch your hamstring while tensing the muscle above your knee at the same time. Repeat with other leg.
exercises.dose: 3 sets of 15 seconds with each leg
notes: Tip: keep your back straight and bend from the hips, you can do the move looking straight ahead or looking straight down.

exercises.name: Heel digs
exercises.ref: How to warm up before exercising · page last reviewed 24 June 2026
exercises.group: How to warm up before exercising
steps: For heel digs, place alternate heels to the front, keeping the front foot pointing up, and punch out with each heel dig. Keep a slight bend in the supporting leg.
exercises.dose: aim for 60 heel digs in 60 seconds

exercises.name: Heel-to-toe walk
exercises.ref: Balance exercises · page last reviewed 7 November 2023
steps: Standing upright, place your right heel on the floor directly in front of your left toe.
Then do the same with your left heel. Make sure you keep looking forward at all times. If necessary, put your fingers against a wall for stability.
exercises.dose: Try to perform at least 5 steps. As you progress, move away from the wall.

exercises.name: Hip marching
exercises.ref: Sitting exercises · page last reviewed 18 January 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Sit upright and do not lean on the back of the chair. Hold on to the sides of the chair.
exercises.about: This exercise will strengthen hips and thighs, and improve flexibility.
steps: Sit upright and do not lean on the back of the chair. Hold on to the sides of the chair.
Lift your left leg with your knee bent as far as is comfortable. Place your foot down with control.
Repeat with the opposite leg.
exercises.dose: Do 5 lifts with each leg.

exercises.name: Inner thigh stretch
exercises.ref: How to stretch after exercising · page last reviewed 16 March 2026
steps: Sit down with your back straight and your legs bent.
Put the soles of your feet together.
Holding on to your feet, try to lower your knees towards the floor.
exercises.dose: hold for 15 to 20 seconds

exercises.name: Knee bends
exercises.ref: How to warm up before exercising · page last reviewed 24 June 2026
exercises.group: How to warm up before exercising
steps: To do knee bends, stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands stretched out. Lower yourself no more than 10cm by bending your knees. Come up and repeat.
exercises.dose: 10 repetitions

exercises.name: Knee lifts
exercises.ref: How to warm up before exercising · page last reviewed 24 June 2026
exercises.group: How to warm up before exercising
steps: To do knee lifts, stand tall and bring up alternate knees to touch the opposite hand. Keep your abs tight and back straight. Keep a slight bend in the supporting leg.
exercises.dose: aim for 30 knee lifts in 30 seconds

exercises.name: Leg extension
exercises.ref: Strength exercises · page last reviewed 28 February 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Rest your hands on the back of a chair for stability.
steps: Rest your hands on the back of a chair for stability.
Standing upright, raise your left leg backwards, keeping it straight. Avoid arching your back as you take your leg back. You should feel the effort in the back of your thigh and bottom.
Repeat with the right leg.
exercises.dose: Hold the lift for up to 5 seconds and repeat 5 times with each leg.

exercises.name: Lunges
exercises.ref: Knee exercises for runners · page last reviewed 20 September 2024
steps: Stand in a split stance with your right leg forward and left leg back.

Slowly bend the knees, lowering into a lunge until the right leg is nearly at a right angle. Keeping the weight on your heels, push back up to the starting position. Keep your back straight and do not let your knees extend over your toes.
exercises.dose: 3 sets of 5 reps with each leg

exercises.name: March on the spot
exercises.ref: How to warm up before exercising · page last reviewed 24 June 2026
exercises.group: How to warm up before exercising
steps: Start off marching on the spot and then march forwards and backwards. Pump your arms up and down in rhythm with your steps, keeping the elbows bent and the fists soft.
exercises.dose: keep going for 3 minutes

exercises.name: Mini-squats
exercises.ref: Strength exercises · page last reviewed 28 February 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Rest your hands on the back of the chair for stability and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
steps: Rest your hands on the back of the chair for stability and stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Slowly bend your knees as far as is comfortable, keeping them facing forwards. Aim to get them over your big toe. Keep your back straight at all times.
Gently come up to standing, squeezing (clenching) your buttocks as you do so.
exercises.dose: Repeat 5 times.

exercises.name: Neck rotation
exercises.ref: Flexibility exercises · page last reviewed 20 November 2023
exercises.about: Improves neck mobility and flexibility.
steps: Sit upright with shoulders down. Look straight ahead.
Slowly turn your head towards your left shoulder as far as is comfortable. Hold for 5 seconds and return to the starting position.
Repeat on the right.
exercises.dose: Do 3 rotations on each side.

exercises.name: Neck stretch
exercises.ref: Flexibility exercises · page last reviewed 20 November 2023
exercises.about: Good for loosening tight neck muscles.
steps: Sitting upright, look straight ahead and hold your left shoulder down with your right hand.
Slowly tilt your head to the right while holding your shoulder down.
Repeat on the opposite side.
exercises.dose: Hold each stretch for 5 seconds and repeat 3 times on each side.

exercises.name: One-leg stand
exercises.ref: Balance exercises · page last reviewed 7 November 2023
exercises.equipment_said: Start by standing facing the wall, with your arms outstretched and your fingertips touching the wall.
steps: Start by standing facing the wall, with your arms outstretched and your fingertips touching the wall.
Lift your left leg, keep your hips level and keep a slight bend in the opposite leg. Gently place your foot back on the floor.
exercises.dose: Hold the lift for 5 to 10 seconds and perform 3 on each side.

exercises.name: Shoulder rolls
exercises.ref: How to warm up before exercising · page last reviewed 24 June 2026
exercises.group: How to warm up before exercising
steps: For shoulder rolls, keep marching on the spot. Roll your shoulders forwards 5 times and backwards 5 times. Let your arms hang loose by your sides.
exercises.dose: 2 sets of 10 repetitions

exercises.name: Sideways bend
exercises.ref: Flexibility exercises · page last reviewed 20 November 2023
exercises.about: Helps restore flexibility to the lower back.
steps: Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart and arms by your sides.
Slide your left arm down your side as far as is comfortable. As you lower your arm, you should feel a stretch on the opposite hip.
Repeat with your right arm.
exercises.dose: Hold each stretch for 2 seconds and perform 3 on each side.

exercises.name: Sideways leg lift
exercises.ref: Strength exercises · page last reviewed 28 February 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Rest your hands on the back of a chair for stability.
steps: Rest your hands on the back of a chair for stability.
Raise your right leg to the side as far as is comfortable, keeping your back and hips straight. Avoid tilting to the right.
Return to the starting position. Now raise your left leg to the side as far as possible.
exercises.dose: Raise and lower each leg 5 times.

exercises.name: Sideways walking
exercises.ref: Balance exercises · page last reviewed 7 November 2023
steps: Stand with your feet together, knees slightly bent.
Step sideways in a slow and controlled manner, moving one foot to the side first.
Move the other to join it.
exercises.dose: Avoid dropping your hips as you step. Perform 10 steps each way or step from one side of the room to the other.

exercises.name: Simple grapevine
exercises.ref: Balance exercises · page last reviewed 7 November 2023
exercises.about: This involves walking sideways by crossing one foot over the other.
steps: Start by crossing your right foot over your left.
Bring your left foot to join it.
exercises.dose: Attempt 5 cross-steps on each side. If necessary, put your fingers against a wall for stability. The smaller the step, the more you work on your balance.

exercises.name: Sit-to-stand
exercises.ref: Strength exercises · page last reviewed 28 February 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Sit on the edge of the chair, feet hip-width apart. Lean slightly forwards.
steps: Sit on the edge of the chair, feet hip-width apart. Lean slightly forwards.
Stand up slowly using your legs, not arms. Keep looking forward and do not look down.
Stand upright and then slowly sit down, using your hands or arms just to guide you if possible .
exercises.dose: Aim for 5 repetitions. The slower the repetitions, the better.

exercises.name: Squats
exercises.ref: Knee exercises for runners · page last reviewed 20 September 2024
steps: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, feet pointing slightly outwards and your hands down by your sides or stretched out in front for extra balance.
Lower yourself as if you're going to sit down, by bending your knees to no more than a right angle. Keep your back straight and do not let your knees go past your toes.

exercises.name: Step-up
exercises.ref: Balance exercises · page last reviewed 7 November 2023
exercises.equipment_said: Use a step, preferably with a railing or near a wall, to use as support.
exercises.about: Use a step, preferably with a railing or near a wall, to use as support.
steps: Step up with your right leg.
Bring your left leg up to join it.
Step down again and return to the start position.
exercises.dose: The key for building balance is to step up and down slowly and in a controlled manner. Perform up to 5 steps with each leg.

exercises.name: Thigh contraction
exercises.ref: Knee exercises for runners · page last reviewed 20 September 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Sit up straight on a chair. Slowly straighten and raise your right leg until straight with your foot pointing slightly outwards.
steps: Sit up straight on a chair. Slowly straighten and raise your right leg until straight with your foot pointing slightly outwards.
Squeeze your right thigh muscles and hold this position for 5 seconds. For the exercise to be effective, you should keep tensing the muscle above your knee. Repeat with the other leg.
exercises.dose: 10 sets of 5 seconds with each leg
notes: Tip: for more of a challenge, perform with an ankle weight

exercises.name: Thigh stretch
exercises.ref: How to stretch after exercising · page last reviewed 16 March 2026
steps: Lie on your right side.
Grab the top of your left foot and gently pull your heel towards your left buttock to stretch the front of the thigh.
Keep your knees touching.
Repeat on the other side.
exercises.dose: hold for 15 to 20 seconds

exercises.name: Upper-body twist
exercises.ref: Sitting exercises · page last reviewed 18 January 2024
exercises.equipment_said: For these exercises, choose a solid, stable chair that does not have wheels.
exercises.about: This stretch will develop and maintain flexibility in the upper back.
steps: Sit upright with your feet flat on the floor, cross your arms and reach for your shoulders.
Without moving your hips, turn your upper body to the left as far as is comfortable. Hold for 5 seconds.
Repeat on the right side.
exercises.dose: Do 5 times on each side.

exercises.name: Wall press-up
exercises.ref: Strength exercises · page last reviewed 28 February 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Stand at arm's length from the wall. Place your hands flat against the wall at chest level, with your fingers pointing upwards.
steps: Stand at arm's length from the wall. Place your hands flat against the wall at chest level, with your fingers pointing upwards.
With your back straight, slowly bend your arms, keeping your elbows by your side. Aim to close the gap between you and the wall as much as you can.
Slowly return to the start.
exercises.dose: Attempt 3 sets of 5 to 10 repetitions.

exercises.name: Wall squats
exercises.ref: Knee exercises for runners · page last reviewed 20 September 2024
exercises.equipment_said: Stand a foot away from a wall with your knees hip-width apart and your feet pointing slightly outwards.
steps: Stand a foot away from a wall with your knees hip-width apart and your feet pointing slightly outwards.

Slide your back down the wall by slowly bending your knees. Do not let your knees go past your toes. Let the knees point in the same direction as your toes. As you come up, focus on tensing the muscle above your knee and your buttocks.
notes: Tip: place an exercise ball between your back and the wall for smooth movement
